evaluations.prompt: Review this FlyDSL fragment without running a GPU: lane = gpu.thread_id("x") % fx.Int64(64); then if const_expr(lane == fx.Int64(0)): store_result(). The kernel has known_block_size=(256,1,1). Write review.md explaining the problem and corrected condition.
expected_behavior: Explains that lane is a runtime SSA value despite known_block_size.
Uses a runtime if condition instead of wrapping the lane comparison in const_expr.
unexpected_behavior: Claims known_block_size makes the current lane a compile-time constant.

evaluations.prompt: Review a FlyDSL software pipeline that uses for iv, state in range(0, 15, 1, init=init_state), creates an LDS view inside the loop, then uses that view in the epilogue. Check the checked-out frontend when determining how init is lowered. No GPU is available. Write review.md with the minimal structural fixes and why they matter.
expected_behavior: Checks the FlyDSL frontend and explains that explicit init selects runtime loop-carried state even with Python integer bounds.
Preserves explicit init and yields updated loop-carried state in the proposed loop structure.
Moves LDS allocation/view creation before the loop so it dominates the epilogue.
unexpected_behavior: Claims the current frontend discards init solely because the bounds are Python integers.
